attributes.risk_rating_note: Cause: leaving the operating conditions (heavy rain, glare, obstruction) is common outdoors and the algorithm may not detect the change → Occ Medium, design is re-used and slightly modified. Det good: dedicated simulation and testing of op-condition changes...
All channels + fusion down at once needs multiple independent faults → Occ Very Low. Total loss of output caught immediately by watchdog within FTT → Det Proven.
Status data-binding; wrong state needs a stale read / race → Occ Low. UI tests cover it but races hard to reproduce → Det Moderate; add state-machine check.
Fixed gain config, no dynamic control → Occ Very Low. Audio level measured against L_alarm_min/max in the test suite → Det Good.

Diverse-redundant sensors fail in different conditions; flat 3-sensor spec, no credited set / min set per condition → Occ Medium. No experiance with the per-modality validity check, so a mismatch (camera credited at night) is possible..
Main detection algo: new data-driven design, no field history → Occ High. Early dev, only nominal-case tests so far → Det Moderate; tasks derived to grow dataset + test coverage.
Simple button→event on a mature UI state machine → Occ Very Low. Failed start immediately visible (no running indicator)...

Bearing/distance maths is the most complex, new part of WarningsSystem → Occ Medium. Edge-case geometry (near-0 distance, ±180°) not fully covered → Det Moderate; directional-accuracy test campaign task.

No safe-state behaviour defined yet → Occ Medium. Undefined reaction can't be verified → Det Limited. This is the runtime response the monitors rely on to avoid single-point faults (detect + safe state, safety impact → QM). Covered here in the risk rating for now; task derived.
Partial channel degradation needs a specific hw fault → Occ Low....
New pipeline but nominal timing holds → Occ Low. Latency measurable in integ test, worst-case load coverage still thin → Det Moderate; timing acceptance-test task derived.
Short deterministic activation path → Occ Low. End-to-end warning test (HiL) on every build → Det Good.
